prompt: Please generate an image. Locked painterly style: hand-painted stylized game art, chunky readable shapes, detail painted not modelled, mid-level detail, softer muted colours with gentle saturation, epic and luminous, never grim. The palette's warm gold and cool teal are painted into the surfaces, but the light is flat, even studio light: no strong key light, no cast shadows, no rim light. Use the attached images only as reference as described: the first attachment is always the style reference for palette and brushwork; later attachments are the approved designs to keep. Game-asset reference sheet for 3D modelling, wide landscape 16:9. Plain light neutral grey background, no scene, no sky, no clouds, no floating rock, no ground plane, a soft contact shadow only. Every piece fully isolated with clear space around it, nothing overlapping, nothing touching the edge, arranged in tidy rows, each with a small neat hand-lettered label underneath. GEAR AND PROPS sheet: Redraw of the attached reference sheet to the current spec: keep the same items and names. For this materials kit a new layout replaces the old one: four rows, one per tier, top to bottom, each row with its tier label at the left; every row has four columns, left to right: the resource node as found in the world, the raw piece, the refined piece, and one flat-on square seamless texture swatch (orthographic, no perspective). The four tiers are the same meshes with a different colour and trim mask, so draw the node, the raw piece and the refined piece with matching shapes in every row, changing only colour, surface and glow. Keep the same tiers and look as the attached sheet. Row 1 "Tier 1 Pale limestone": "Pale limestone outcrop", a waist-high quarry outcrop of soft parchment-cream stone with chisel marks (about 1.2 m); "Pale limestone rough block", a rough-broken block (about 40 cm); "Pale limestone cut block", a clean squared block with chisel marks (about 40 cm); "Pale limestone texture". Row 2 "Tier 2 Cragslate": "Cragslate outcrop", the same outcrop shape in hard dark grey slate splitting into layered sheets; "Cragslate rough block", split along its layers; "Cragslate cut block", a clean block with visible layer lines; "Cragslate texture". Row 3 "Tier 3 Glimmerstone": "Glimmerstone outcrop", the same outcrop shape in dark stone with bright teal crystal veins glowing softly; "Glimmerstone rough block"; "Glimmerstone cut block", teal veins glowing; "Glimmerstone texture". Row 4 "Tier 4 Ruinstone": "Ruinstone ruin", the same outcrop silhouette as a broken heap of smooth pale old-world worked stone with precise bevelled edges and engraved concentric ring patterns, half sunk in moss (ruinstone is salvaged from ruins, never quarried; no columns, no classical carving); "Ruinstone fragment", a broken worked piece with precise bevels; "Ruinstone cut block", precise and smooth with an engraved ring motif; "Ruinstone texture". Each tier label is exactly "Tier 1 Pale limestone", "Tier 2 Cragslate", "Tier 3 Glimmerstone", "Tier 4 Ruinstone": no taglines, no extra words anywhere. Cragslate is plain dark grey with no rust colour; the glimmerstone glow is soft and kept to the veins; no moss on the pale limestone or on any texture swatch. No crafted items, no extra pieces. Outcrops stand at true scale to the scale figure; the smaller blocks are drawn enlarged for legibility and carry their real size in the label. Each item alone in three-quarter front view, in rows by family or tier, with thick chunky proportions: thick blades, solid rope, chunky grips, no thin parts. A plain neutral 1.8 m human silhouette labelled "1.8 m" stands on the sheet for scale, with everything at true scale to it. Title at the top: "Materials kit: stones".
